What Lightning Search is

Lightning Search finds sounds in your library from inside Reaper as fast as you can type, lets you hear them through Reaper, and puts them on the timeline with one key.

It has two components:

  • The search window in Reaper. A Reaper script you open with a shortcut. You type, the results update dynamically, and you can listen through detected variations with the arrow keys. Press Enter to spot a sound at the edit cursor.
  • The helper. A small program in the Windows notification area (the tray, by the clock), or in the menu bar on a Mac. It reads your library folders once, keeps a search index of them, and keeps that index up to date as files are added, changed or removed.

Lightning Search reads the metadata already embedded in your files (by Soundminer, BaseHead, Reaper’s Media Explorer and similar tools): file name, description, category and CatID, keywords, library, designer, etc. It never writes to your files and does not edit metadata.

On a Mac, this guide’s keys change the way Reaper’s do: Cmd where it says Ctrl, and Cmd+Opt where it says Alt (Option on its own types a character). Control+click works as a right-click. The tray is the menu bar icon, and Explorer is Finder. The Shortcuts table lists both systems’ keys.

Requirements

  • Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, or macOS 11 Big Sur or newer (Apple silicon or Intel).
  • Reaper 5.982 or newer (any edition, installed or portable).
  • The SWS extension, version 2.14 or newer: https://www.sws-extension.org.
  • ReaImGui, version 0.9 or newer, installed through ReaPack (Extensions > ReaPack > Browse packages, search for ReaImGui).
  • Sound files in WAV, Broadcast WAV, RF64, Wave64, AIFF or FLAC.

Installing

On Windows

  1. Download LightningSearch-0.9.1-beta-Windows-setup.exe from the Gumroad page.

  2. Run it. The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may show “Windows protected your PC”. Click More info, then Run anyway. Some browsers also ask whether to keep the download: choose Keep.

  3. The installer finds your Reaper resource folders: the usual one, a portable Reaper that Reaper’s installer set up, and any folder an earlier install used. Tick each Reaper you want Lightning Search in; Add a Reaper folder… picks another folder (the one that holds reaper.ini; in Reaper, Options > Show REAPER resource path opens it). Next stays greyed out until a folder is ticked.

  4. It checks for SWS and ReaImGui in each folder and says which are missing. You can still install and add them afterwards.

  5. If Reaper is running, the installer asks you to close it first.

  6. On the last page, Start Lightning Search now starts the helper and opens its welcome window.

Lightning Search installs for your Windows user only, so it needs no administrator rights. The program goes in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Lightning Search; in each Reaper folder it adds UserPlugins\reaper_lightning.dll and Scripts\Lightning Search\. The next time Reaper starts, it adds the Lightning Search actions to the Action List by itself.

To update, run a newer installer over the old one. Your library index, settings, favorites and playlists stay intact.

On a Mac

  1. Open Reaper once if you never have, so its settings folder exists, then quit it.

  2. Download LightningSearch-0.9.1-beta-macOS.dmg from the Gumroad page, open it and drag Lightning Search onto Applications.

  3. Open Lightning Search from Applications. It is not notarised by Apple yet, so the first time macOS says it was not opened. Click Done, then open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to “Lightning Search was blocked” and click Open Anyway (macOS asks for your password). On macOS 14 and older, Control-click the app in Applications and choose Open instead. macOS remembers this; you do it once.

  4. The lightning icon appears in the menu bar and the welcome window opens. The app copies reaper_lightning.dylib into UserPlugins and the scripts into Scripts/Lightning Search/ in Reaper’s folder (~/Library/Application Support/REAPER).

  5. Start Reaper (or quit and reopen it if it was open). It adds the Lightning Search actions to the Action List by itself. The welcome window’s last page says the same.

To update, drag the newer app over the old one in Applications and open it: it updates Reaper’s copy by itself, and Reaper picks it up the next time it starts.

First run

The helper’s welcome window walks through three steps:

  1. Add your library folders. Click Add library folder… and pick each folder that holds sounds. External and network drives work; when one is unplugged its sounds stay in the index, marked offline. Remove takes out a folder added by mistake.

  2. Start scanning. The helper reads the metadata of every file. The progress page shows how many sounds it has found, how many are searchable already, and an estimate of the time left. You can search while it scans: results grow as it goes. A large library takes a while the first time; after that, only changes are read.

  3. Open Lightning Search in Reaper. In Reaper, choose Actions > Show action list, type Lightning_Search and run Script: Lightning_Search.lua. To open it with a key, select it, click Add… under Shortcuts and press the keys.

The helper then sits in the tray (the menu bar on a Mac) and starts with Windows (at login on a Mac), so it is always ready when Reaper is. You can turn that off in the helper’s settings or the tray menu.

The core loop

  1. Press your shortcut. The search window opens with the cursor in the search box.
  2. Type. Results update on every key.
  3. Use the up/down arrow keys or click to select sounds to audition.
  4. Press Enter. The sound lands at the edit cursor on the selected track, and the window collapses to the search bar and waveform (Settings > General can hide it instead).

Click the ? icon by the cog at any time for a cheat sheet of every key, with your own shortcuts filled in.

Searching

Type words and Lightning Search finds sounds whose name or metadata holds all of them. The last word matches as you type it: expl already finds explosions.

Ctrl+F or Tab goes back to the search box from anywhere in the window with the whole search selected, so typing replaces it. Typing a letter that is not a shortcut while the results have the keyboard adds it to the search. Your Reaper shortcut for Lightning Search does what Settings > Visibility > “Shortcut while the window has focus” says when the window already has focus, and selects the search whenever the window stays open.

The clock button left of the search box lists your recent searches (the ones you picked a sound from since Reaper started); click one to run it again, or clear the list.

Type Finds
metal door sounds with both words, anywhere in their name or metadata
metal, wood sounds with either word (a comma means “or”)
-wood hides sounds that have the word
"glass break" the words side by side, in that order
impact (metal, wood) brackets group words: metal impact or wood impact
crash* crash, crashes, crashing… (a star at the end of one word)

Find every ending (Settings > Search, on by default) adds the star’s functionality to every search term, so crash also finds crashes and crashing.

Spellcheck underlines a word that neither your library nor the dictionary knows, in grey, once you type a space or comma after it (and every word once you click away from the search box, or when nothing is found). The underline turns yellow while there are no results. Right-click an underlined word for corrections: words from your own library come first. Turn it off with Settings > Search > “Check spelling”. Words in your files’ metadata, filenames and library names count as known, so the spellcheck learns your library’s vocabulary.

Fields searched (Settings > Search) picks the details plain words look in. By default that’s the FX name, description, keywords, notes, category, subcategory, file name and library. Tick Designer, Microphone or any other detail to search it too; File path searches the names of the folders a sound is in, so cinematic finds every sound in a “Cinematic Metal” folder. Its matches rank below description and FX name matches, so the sounds you found before keep their order. Untick a detail to stop plain words finding it. A name and a colon (designer:smith, below) still searches any one detail, whatever is ticked.

Searching one detail

A name and a colon searches just that detail:

Type Searches
lib:boom or library:"Boom Library" the library name
cat:door the UCS category or subcategory
catid:DOORWood the exact CatID
desc:, kw:, filename:, fx:, designer:, mfr:, recordist:, mic:, notes:, subcat: description, keywords, file name, FX name, designer, manufacturer, recordist, microphone, notes, subcategory
dur:1s..5s, dur:<500ms, dur:>2m length (ms, s, m, h; a bare number is seconds)
ch:stereo, ch:mono, ch:>2 channel count
sr:48k, sr:44.1k..96k sample rate
bits:>=24 bit depth
type:flac, type:wav file type
vars:1, vars:>=10, vars:2..5 how many separate sounds (variations) the file holds
created:2024, modified:..2023-12-31 file dates (a year or month covers all of it)

Numbers and dates take >, >=, <, <= and ranges written a..b, a.. or ..b.

Thesaurus

The book button (Alt+T) turns the thesaurus on or off. With it on, helicopter also finds files that only say chopper or heli, ranked below the files that say helicopter. The line under the search box lists the extra words it searched. Settings > Search chooses the sources (word forms, UCS categories, sound design synonyms, your own groups) and lets you add your own groups or import a Soundminer .tth thesaurus. UCS categories start off; turn them on there to have chopper also find files with the CatID AEROHeli.

Filters and sorting

The funnel button opens filters for file type, sample rate, bit depth, channels, length and variations. Each filter shows as a chip by the search box; its x removes it. Click a column header to sort by it, again to reverse, and a third time to go back to relevance.

Databases

The dropdown at the left of the search box picks a database: a named set of library folders to search, such as “Foley” or “Creatures”. All folders searches everything. Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 pick the first nine databases in the list. Make and edit them in Settings > Databases (or the helper’s settings window). “Add a folder to …” at the end of the dropdown adds a folder to the picked database. Adding a folder opens Explorer’s (or Finder’s) folder picker.

Listening

  • Down / Up move through the results and play each one; Page Down / Page Up move a page at a time.

  • Space plays or stops the highlighted sound.

  • Click the bottom half of the waveform to play a variation from its start, or the top half to play from that point; drag across it to pick a range without playing it. A picked range is what Space plays and what gets added. Settings > Workflow > “Clicking the waveform” has other ways.

  • Left / Right step through a sound’s variations: the separate hits inside one file. “Skip initial silence” (Settings > Audition, on by default) starts each sound at its first variation. The Variation detection panel (its button sits under the waveform) sets how loud a hit must be and how long a gap separates two.

  • The channel list under the waveform, right of Pitch, plays one channel or several of a stereo, surround or multi-mic file. Channels are named from the file when it names them (L, R, C, LFE, Ls, Rs, or mic names), and each waveform lane shows its name. Selecting another result starts it on all channels again.

  • The small channel buttons before the list do the same with one click: click a channel to hear it alone (click it again for all channels), Shift+click to add or remove one, and right-click any of them to go back to all channels. With none lit, every channel plays.

  • With several sounds selected, Play together under the waveform plays them at once as one sound, aligned at the start, a channel each: handy for one take recorded on several mics. Use the channel list to solo a mic or pick a few. Up to 8 channels in all, at one sample rate. Any other selection turns it off again.

  • Reverse (R), the channel pick and Pitch also apply to what you add to the project. Loop (L) and Volume are only for listening.

  • A playing sound follows Pitch while you drag it. Turn off “Live Pitch” in Settings > Audition to have it change speed only when you let go.

  • FX (F) plays sounds through the selected track’s effects and fader, so you hear them as they will sound in the mix. Settings > Audition can send them through a dedicated “Lightning Search FX” track instead.

  • Sync (Y) plays the sound with Reaper’s transport, starting a pre-roll before the edit cursor, so you hear it in place against picture and other tracks. Reaper’s own Play and Stop work too while Sync is on.

Lightning Search plays sounds through Reaper itself, on hidden audition tracks, so they come out of your usual audio device.

Adding sounds to the project

  • Enter adds the highlighted sound at the edit cursor on the selected track. With no track selected, it makes a new track for it after the last track in the project.
  • New track (Ctrl+T) puts each sound on its own new track below the selected one, named after the sound. While it is on with Sync or FX on too, an empty track shows where the next one will go, so auditions can play there; it disappears when you turn those off or close the window. Click that track to put effects on it: it stays where it is while selected, auditions play through its effects with FX on, and Enter then adds the sound onto it (or, with no effects on it, makes the new track in its place). With FX on, that empty track is selected as it appears, so an FX browser puts effects straight onto it. Settings > Workflow > “New track takes the selected track’s color” colors the new track like the selected one.
  • With New track on and an empty track selected (no items and no effects), Enter adds the sound onto that track instead of making another one below it; an unnamed track takes the sound’s name. Turn this off with Settings > Workflow > “New track uses the selected track when it is empty”.
  • Ctrl+click or Shift+click picks several results; Enter adds them one after another. With Play together on, Enter puts each one on a new track of its own instead, all starting at the edit cursor.
  • Settings > Workflow picks how you place sounds:
    • Spotting (the default): keys add at the edit cursor, and you can right-drag the waveform onto a track.
    • Drag to timeline: drag results straight from the list onto a track; the window folds away so you can see where you drop.
  • Ctrl+E opens the sound in the primary external editor set in Reaper’s Preferences > External Editors (Ctrl+Shift+E: the secondary one); the result’s right-click menu names both. Settings > Workflow > “Opening in an editor” picks what opens: a copy kept in Lightning Search’s own folder (the default, so your library is never changed), a copy Reaper adds to the project (saving updates that item), or the library file itself.
  • Each addition is one undo step in Reaper (Ctrl+Z), including any track it made.

Lightning Search never copies or converts files: items point at your library files where they are.

Favorites, playlists and databases

  • B (or the star at the start of a row) adds the highlighted sound to Favorites.
  • The panel button at the left of the search bar shows the sidebar: Library, Favorites and your folders and playlists. Right-click it for New playlist and New folder.
  • Right-click results for Add to playlist, or drag results onto a playlist in the sidebar.
  • Right-click results and pick Hide to keep sounds you never want out of your searches (favorites and playlists still show them). Settings > Hidden lists them and puts them back; its Hide offline files switch leaves out sounds on drives that are not connected.
  • Clicking a playlist searches inside it. With the search box empty it shows the playlist in its own order, and you can drag rows to reorder or press Delete to remove them.
  • A sound whose file has gone shows greyed out with its old name, so you can see what was there.
  • Favorites and playlists are kept by the helper and survive rescans, index rebuilds and updates.
  • The details panel (Ctrl+I) shows all of a sound’s metadata and its embedded artwork.
  • Click a word in the details panel to show only sounds with that word in that field; click a field’s title (Description, Designer, …) to match its whole value; click a folder in the Path to show that folder and every folder in it. The search box keeps what you typed. Each of these shows as a chip under the search bar (click it to take it off), and Clear details filter takes them all off.

Settings

Open them with the cog in the search window. Every change applies at once. Each tab has Reset to defaults for that tab only.

Tab What it holds
General What the open shortcut, Esc, clicking outside and Enter do to the window (hide it, collapse it to the search bar, or collapse it to the search bar and waveform); docking and always on top; tooltips; the update check; About (versions); third-party notices; Report a bug or send feedback
Search Find every ending; Check spelling; Fields searched; the thesaurus on or off, its sources and your own groups
Audition Play on click; play while paging; Live Pitch; skip initial silence; waveform channels; pitch reset; where FX plays through; the sync pre-roll
Workflow Spotting or Drag to timeline; the gap between sounds added together; what the external editor opens; what clicking the waveform plays; New track’s color; New track using an empty selected track
Shortcuts Two shortcuts per action, each a key or a middle or side mouse button with Ctrl, Shift or Alt; right-click a box to clear it
Databases Your databases and the folders in each
Hidden Hide offline files; the sounds you hid, each with Show again
Appearance Text size and row height
Colors The window’s colours (the title bar in and out of focus too), the waveform, the playback cursor and the spelling underlines

The helper has its own settings window (click the tray icon): library folders and databases, how it keeps up with changes (live watching, or a daily check at a time you pick), scanning in the background at low priority, starting with Windows, the update check, and where its data lives.

Shortcuts

These are the search window’s default keys. Change any of them in Settings > Shortcuts. On a Mac, keys held with Control (rather than Cmd) are left to Reaper: the window neither uses them nor records them as shortcuts.

Action Windows Mac
Next result Down Down
Previous result Up Up
Page down Page Down Page Down
Page up Page Up Page Up
Random result Alt+R Cmd+Opt+R
Add to the timeline Enter Enter
Play / stop Space Space
Previous variation Left Left
Next variation Right Right
Add to favorites B B
Remove from playlist Delete Cmd+Backspace
Audition through track FX F F
Sync with playback Y Y
Loop L L
Reverse R R
Search box Ctrl+F or Tab Cmd+F or Tab
New track option Ctrl+T Cmd+T
Thesaurus on/off Alt+T Cmd+Opt+T
Details panel Ctrl+I Cmd+I
Open in primary external editor Ctrl+E Cmd+E
Open in secondary external editor Ctrl+Shift+E Cmd+Shift+E
Database 1 to 9 in the list Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 Cmd+1 to Cmd+9

Opening the window, adding the highlighted sound, auditioning it and moving through the results are also Reaper actions (Script: Lightning_Search.lua, Lightning_Commit.lua, Lightning_Audition.lua, Lightning_Next_Result.lua, Lightning_Previous_Result.lua and Lightning_Random_Result.lua), so you can give them keys in Reaper’s Action List that work even when the search window is not focused. Random result picks one of the 500 best-ranked matches.

Privacy

  • Your library, its index, your searches, favorites and playlists stay on your computer. Lightning Search has no account, no analytics and no usage tracking.
  • The update check (once a day; Settings > General can turn it off) downloads one small file from gla1wo.github.io saying what the newest version is. It sends nothing about you or your library.
  • Bug reports You see everything in the report before it is made, and you choose whether to attach it to the form. Library folders become <library 1>, other paths become <path>, and your user name, computer name and email addresses are removed. Searches and metadata never appear in the logs.

Lightning Search keeps its data in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lightning (on a Mac, ~/Library/Application Support/Lightning): the catalogue and index, favorites and playlists, your thesaurus, logs and reports. The search window’s own settings live in Reaper’s reaper-extstate.ini.

Troubleshooting

“The helper isn’t running.” Start Lightning Search from the Start menu (from Applications on a Mac); the search window connects by itself. If it keeps stopping, send a bug report (below): it includes any crash notes.

A drive shows as offline. Its sounds stay listed, greyed and marked offline, until the drive is back. When it is, the helper checks it for changes by itself. To drop a drive you no longer use, remove its folder in the helper’s settings.

New files don’t show up. With live watching (the default), changes appear within about a minute. Network drives may not report changes: use Rescan now in the tray menu, or switch to a daily check in the helper’s settings.

The first scan takes a while. Reading every file’s metadata takes time on large libraries, especially on USB or network drives. You can search while it runs. “Scan in the background” keeps it at low priority so Reaper never stutters; you can pause it from the tray menu.

Antivirus. Some antivirus tools briefly lock files Lightning Search is writing to its index; the helper waits and tries again. If your antivirus quarantines or blocks lightning-helper.exe or the installer, allow them.

Lightning Search is missing from Reaper’s Action List. Restart Reaper once after installing. If it is still missing, load Scripts\Lightning Search\scripts\Lightning_Search.lua with New action > Load ReaScript… in the Action List. On a Mac, if the scripts never arrived (the helper’s log says “Reaper’s resource folder was not found”), open Reaper once, quit it, then quit and reopen Lightning Search from the menu bar.

Mac: “Lightning Search Not Opened”. See Installing on a Mac: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway, once.

Mac: two sounds whose names differ only in capitals. On a case-sensitive drive (rare; macOS’s own drives are not), Kick.wav and kick.wav in the same folder show as one result. Rename one of them.

“ReaImGui is missing” or “SWS is missing”. Install them (see Requirements) and restart Reaper.

No sound when auditioning. Check Reaper’s audio device is running (Options > Audio device) and that its master output is not muted. Auditions play through Reaper.

Reporting a bug or sending feedback

Use Report a bug or send feedback… in the tray menu, or in the search window under Settings > General.

  1. Choose Bug, Idea or Other and write what happened.
  2. Show what will be sent shows the whole report.
  3. Create report saves a zip in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lightning\reports (the Mac: ~/Library/Application Support/Lightning/reports), shows it in Explorer or Finder and opens the feedback form in your browser. Paste your message there and attach the zip. The form needs a Google sign-in to upload files.

Uninstalling

On Windows

Open Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find Lightning Search and choose Uninstall. It closes the helper, removes the program and the Reaper files it added, and takes its actions out of Reaper’s Action List. It asks whether to keep your library index, favorites, playlists and settings, in case you install again; choose No to remove them too.

On a Mac

Quit Reaper, then choose Uninstall Lightning Search… in the menu bar menu. It takes the Lightning Search actions out of Reaper’s Action List, removes the extension and scripts it added to Reaper, stops it starting at login, and asks whether to keep your library index, favorites, playlists and settings; choose Delete to remove them too. Then drag Lightning Search from Applications to the Trash.
